does: Cooks delicate food gently in liquid that is hot but never boils.
how: Heat the liquid until it trembles, with small bubbles on the bottom of the pan and almost none rising.
Hold the heat there. Turn it down the moment bubbles start to break the surface.
Lift the food out with a slotted spoon and drain it well.
For an egg, add a little vinegar to the water, crack the egg into a small bowl first, and tip it in at the surface.

cues.text: The surface shivers and steams, and nothing rolls.
A poached egg feels like a soft cushion when pressed: the white is set and the yolk is loose inside.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the liquid boil, which tears an egg apart and toughens fish and chicken.
mistakes.fix: Turn the heat down, or add a splash of cold liquid.

mistakes.mistake: Using an old egg, whose thin white spreads into rags.
mistakes.fix: Use the freshest eggs you have, and drain off the watery part of the white through a sieve.

comes_after.why: Poaching sits just under a simmer, so a cook has to be able to find a simmer first.
